name: Cognoscere / Lumira
currentPhase: Product validation, OKF contracts and authenticated service architecture
portfolioRole: The major product: a broad platform where knowledge modelling, pedagogy, social systems and governed intelligence meet.
headline: A competency-oriented learning environment whose content, evidence and social activity keep their own meaning.

relationship.cognoscere: The educational intelligence, pedagogical knowledge and competency structure.
relationship.lumira: The social and educational web platform through which students, teachers and schools interact with Cognoscere.

challenge: Learning platforms can collapse content, scores, social activity and competition into interchangeable points. That weakens pedagogical meaning and makes evidence difficult to trace.
productResponse: Cognoscere/Lumira separates competency progression, social reputation and competition while connecting courses, BNCC skills, materials, open activities, communities, schools and teacher-mediated evidence.

actors.name: Student
actors.responsibility: Enrol, study, answer, participate, submit and build a visible learning profile.

actors.name: Approved teacher
actors.responsibility: Create pedagogical contexts, evaluate evidence, moderate and produce authorised reports.

actors.name: School administration
actors.responsibility: Manage teachers, classes, communities, competitions and institutional visibility.

actors.name: Platform administration
actors.responsibility: Govern BNCC domains, schools, plans, moderation and audit.

independentDomains.name: Competency progression
independentDomains.rule: Changes through quizzes and pedagogical evidence. Social votes and leaderboards do not directly alter competency.

independentDomains.name: Social reputation
independentDomains.rule: Represents contributions in communities and profiles while remaining distinct from learning level.

independentDomains.name: School competition
independentDomains.rule: Represents performance within a challenge. Teacher-confirmed evidence may separately affect competency.

productLayers.name: Public entry
productLayers.description: Proposition, areas, courses, competitions, profiles, plans and enrolment.

productLayers.name: Personal campus
productLayers.description: Progress, next actions, course discovery, quizzes and social presence.

productLayers.name: Learning path
productLayers.description: Course, cycles, axes, continuous material, open activity, evidence and progression.

productLayers.name: Community
productLayers.description: Forums, posts, comments, votes, reputation, school and group contexts.

productLayers.name: School challenges
productLayers.description: Brief, deadline, submission, rubric, teacher evaluation and leaderboard.

productLayers.name: Knowledge infrastructure
productLayers.description: Technical OKF, editorial review, public projection, provenance and protected intelligence.

implemented: Static Vite SPA prototype with public landing and responsive campus
Public OKF manifest and client for course, skill, material, activity and provenance
Catalogue, course, axis and continuous material navigation
Local demonstrative pre-analysis of open responses
Forum, competition, profile, school and account surfaces
Desktop full-width campus and mobile social drawer validation
boundaries: The public projection does not include private rubrics, reference answers, administrative prompts or identifiable student data.
The current browser pre-analysis is demonstrative and does not replace teacher or pedagogical confirmation.
Authentication, persistence, moderation and production payment remain future service layers.
architectureFlow: Ruby exporter and canonical technical prompts
evidence: Course catalogue resolves a public OKF manifest rather than silently hardcoding curriculum fallback.
Desktop and mobile journeys were reviewed across public entry, enrolment, quiz, course, forum, competition, profile and account surfaces.
The product explicitly separates competence, reputation and leaderboard semantics.
Public and protected intelligence boundaries are described in the product and repository contracts.
roadmap: Student response, evidence and progression persistence
Protected model analysis with teacher confirmation
Moderation, reporting, blocking, rate limits and audit trails
Production subscription and payment provider adapter
